previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 65-year-old man with a history of histiocytosis X and diabetes insipidus was admitted for elective resection of a left temporal brain mass. MRI showed significant growth of the lesion, and he underwent a left temporal craniotomy. Postoperatively, he developed expressive aphasia, which gradually improved. Pathology confirmed high-grade B-cell central nervous system lymphoma. Workup included a right inguinal lymph node biopsy and bone marrow biopsy to rule out systemic disease; early findings suggested the lymphoma was confined to the CNS. He received cycle one of high-dose methotrexate chemotherapy, tolerated it well, and required leucovorin and sodium bicarbonate for drug clearance. Hyponatremia, likely due to SIADH and hydrochlorothiazide, resolved with medication adjustments and salt supplementation. DDAVP was held temporarily and restarted as sodium stabilized. He was discharged home with outpatient follow-up, speech therapy, and a plan for further chemotherapy.

not confirm malignancy, but suggest a abnormal 
lymphoproliferation.  Craniotomy was complicated by a severe 
aphasia, which improved over the week.  Now his speech is back 
to normal and he feels well.  Presenting symptoms have cleared.  
He noted mild nausea after cycle #1.
